strengths: Gap bars maintain 3/4 meter and quarter-note rhythmic vocabulary consistent with surrounding material
Bass descent d-B-G in bar 6 echoes the tonic arpeggiation pattern of bars 1-2 and 9-10
Bar 7's A3 dominant preparation follows logically from the implied G major harmony of bar 6
issues: Bar 5's c-e-g overwrites the soprano register with a lower-octave figure that breaks the consistent upper-voice trajectory established in bars 1-4 and 9-12
The leap to d-B-G in bar 6 creates a registral drop and textural thinning without the characteristic baroque two-voice implication present in adjacent phrases
Missing chromatic or leading-tone element in bar 6 (no F#) weakens the dominant preparation compared to bar 8's A3 which functions as V/V
suggestions: Raise bar 5 to c'-e'-g' to maintain the upper register established in parallel bars 1 and 9
Add an inner voice or modify bar 6 to include F# (e.g., d B F# or d/f# B G) to strengthen the dominant function leading to bar 7
Consider d'-b-g for bar 6 to preserve the register and create smoother voice-leading connection to the A3 in bar 7
critic.summary: The gap bars function adequately in harmonic and rhythmic terms but suffer from a registral inconsistency in bar 5 and insufficient dominant preparation in bar 6; with register adjustment and added leading-tone, they would seamlessly integrate into the baroque minuet style.
